title: prefill-stride-and-kernel-choreo-harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a new harness that exercises combinations of kernel selection policies, attention window micro-variants, and prefill->decode stride schedules to produce robust golden baselines and CI perf gates that are resilient to non-determinism and realistic tail workloads.
background: Current benchmark suites focus on single-dimension experiments (e.g., kernel routing or prefill pacing) which miss correlated regressions that occur when kernel swaps interact with attention optimization heuristics and prefill scheduling. We see intermittent tail increases in prod when new kernel heuristics are introduced and the current CI gates are noisy because golden baselines do not cover cohort-level variance or mixed-mode traffic.
proposed_solution: Build a modular harness ('choreo-harness') that: (1) generates synthetic cohorts by replaying sampled production traces with controlled noise injection, (2) exercises a matrix of kernel-routing policies x attention-window variants x prefill stride schedules, (3) records token-level latency distributions and KV/cache hit patterns, (4) produces delta-golden artifacts with confidence intervals and probabilistic flakiness scores, and (5) integrates with CI to create automated perf gates that support soft-fails and staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can synthesize at least 6 distinct workload cohorts representative of short-chat, long-prefill, streaming, and mixed-latency traffic
End-to-end runs produce repeatable delta reports with 95th/99th quantile cost and latency plus inferred root-cause tags (kernel vs scheduling vs attention)
CI integration returns deterministic pass/fail at configured sensitivity (e.g., 95% confidence on 5% delta) and produces human-readable remediation hints
Golden baseline lockfile format is compact and supports incremental updates without invalidating unrelated cohorts
Dashboard ingestion pipeline shows cohort enumerations, historical deltas, and an automated rollback suggestion when a gate fails
milestones: M2: harness core: workload generator + matrix runner (2026-02-19)
M3: diagnostics: root-cause tagging and delta reporter (2026-03-05)
M4: CI adaptor + perf gate config (2026-03-22)
M5: dashboard + rollout runbook + initial golden commit (2026-03-29)
test_plan: Use a blend of (a) replayed production traces (anonymized) sampled across customers, (b) synthetic microbench cases for attention patterns (sliding windows, sparse vs dense attention), and (c) stress cases that force kernel swaps under prefill pressure. Each experiment will run 10 seeds with controlled RNG variance; report aggregate quantiles and inter-seed variance. Establish gate thresholds using historical delta distributions and calibrate sensitivity to ~2x current false-positive rate.
risks: High compute cost for matrix runs; noisy signals from upstream trace sampling; potential for overfitting golden baselines to synthetic cohorts. Mitigations include adaptive sampling, early-exit heuristics for runs, and tiered goldens (stable vs experimental).
runbook_notes: When a CI perf gate fails, automated job posts a diagnostic artifact (delta-report + top-3 suspected causes) and pins the failing commit to a canary rollout with a throttled traffic fraction. On repeated failures, trigger an oncall paging path and toast a rollback playbook link.
